name: Confirm and settle power and gas trades with counterparties
summary: When the trading desk sells future output or buys gas, the back office must confirm that the counterparty agrees every term of the trade and, after delivery, settle the money. Settlement analysts match each trade with the exchange report, an electronic confirmation service or a paper confirmation, chase the breaks with traders and counterparties, then after each delivery month prepare netting statements, compare them with the counterparty's, approve payments and post the entries. Unconfirmed or mis-booked trades create credit and accounting risk, and month-end bunches several hundred settlements into a few days.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator hedging about half of its capacity with forward power and gas trades, cleared on NGX or ICE or traded bilaterally under EEI, ISDA and GasEDI master agreements.
baseline.notes: One trade is followed through confirmation and the settlement of its first delivery month; later months of a strip are settled in the same monthly runs.

trigger: A trade is booked in the ETRM system by a trader or arrives from the exchange trade feed.
end_state: The trade is confirmed and its first delivery month has been settled in cash and posted to the ledger, or it has been cancelled after a dispute.

volume.seasonality: More trades in the months before winter and summer peaks and in volatile price periods; settlement work peaks in the first ten business days of each month.

surge.cause: price spike or cold snap that triggers re-hedging and short-term balancing trades (for example February 2021)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from desk practice; no opened source gives trade counts.

Organisation file demand driver dd_trades, itself an estimate; the AIF's statement that about 50 percent of capacity is contracted and merchant positions are hedged regularly supports a large trade flow but gives no count.

systems.name: Energy trading and risk management system
Exchange and broker trading screens (NGX, ICE)
AESO Energy Trading System (offers, declarations and dispatch)
ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)

steps.name: Capture the trade in the ETRM system
steps.description: The trader's deal, or the exchange trade feed, creates a trade record in the energy trading and risk management system, which assigns a deal number, checks mandatory fields and places the trade in the back-office confirmation queue.

evidence.note: Standard ETRM trade capture; the trader's own booking time belongs to the hedging process.

steps.name: Check the trade capture against the deal evidence
steps.description: A settlement analyst compares the ETRM record with the trader's ticket, broker recap or exchange trade report, checking counterparty, buy or sell, product, volume, price, delivery period, delivery point and master agreement, and sends booking errors back to the trader.

error.defect_description: A booking error in price, volume or delivery period is missed.

control.basis: Risk management policy: trade confirmation and settlement by a back office independent of the traders

evidence.note: Channel shares estimated: Alberta forward power and gas are largely cleared on NGX, larger counterparties use electronic matching, the rest exchange PDF confirmations.

steps.name: Match the trade to the exchange trade report
steps.description: The analyst ties each exchange-cleared trade to the exchange's end-of-day trade and clearing report; a matched exchange trade needs no bilateral confirmation because the clearing house is the counterparty.

control.basis: Risk management policy: trade confirmation and settlement by a back office independent of the traders

next.condition: break between ETRM and exchange report

evidence.note: Batch wait reflects the end-of-day exchange report; match rate estimated.

steps.name: Submit the trade to electronic confirmation matching
steps.description: The ETRM system sends the trade to ICE eConfirm, whose matching engine compares it with the counterparty's or broker's submission and returns a matched or unmatched status to the back office.

next.condition: unmatched or counterparty did not submit

evidence.note: Electronic matching for on- and off-exchange energy trades from the ICE fact sheet; the vendor's 95 percent match within minutes is lowered to 92 percent to allow late counterparty submissions.

steps.name: Draft the outgoing confirmation
steps.description: The analyst generates a confirmation from the ETRM template under the governing master agreement (EEI, ISDA or GasEDI), adds any special terms such as shaped volumes, delivery points or option features, and checks it against the trade record.

error.defect_description: A special term is left out of the confirmation.

evidence.note: Paper confirmation practice estimated.

steps.name: Sign the outgoing confirmation
steps.description: The manager of settlement and contracts, as an authorised signatory, reviews non-standard terms on the confirmation, signs it and the analyst sends it to the counterparty by email.

control.basis: Delegation of authority and authorised signatory list for trading confirmations

evidence.note: Signatory practice estimated.

steps.name: Receive and compare the counterparty's confirmation
steps.description: The analyst waits for the counterparty to countersign or send its own confirmation, then compares every economic term with the ETRM record and the outgoing confirmation and records the confirmation as matched or disputed.

control.basis: Risk management policy: trade confirmation and settlement by a back office independent of the traders

next.condition: terms differ or confirmation not returned

evidence.note: Counterparty turnaround and mismatch rate estimated.

steps.name: Investigate the confirmation break
steps.description: The analyst compares the broker recap, chat or recorded line notes and both parties' records to find which term differs, and contacts the counterparty's or exchange's back office to compare records.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Trader confirms the intended terms
steps.description: The term trader who executed the deal states the agreed terms, checks the recorded line if needed, and amends the ETRM booking if the company's record is wrong or asks the counterparty's trader to have their side corrected.

next.condition: company booking wrong, amended and rechecked

evidence.note: Split estimated.

steps.name: Escalate a disputed trade
steps.description: The manager reviews the evidence, including recorded calls and broker records, discusses the disputed terms with the counterparty's back-office manager and the trading director, and agrees an amendment, a settlement of the difference or cancellation.

next.condition: trade cancelled or difference paid out

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Feed confirmation status to credit and risk reports
steps.description: The confirmed trade, with its mark-to-market exposure, flows from the ETRM system into the daily credit exposure and risk reports used by the credit and risk teams, and trades unconfirmed after the policy deadline appear on an ageing report.

evidence.note: The AIF says the company monitors trading so counterparty credit limits are not exceeded and posts collateral above credit limits; the automated feed is the author's description.

steps.name: Actualise volumes and prices after delivery
steps.description: After the delivery month ends the analyst confirms delivered volumes (net settlement instructions in the AESO system for physical power, pipeline allocations for physical gas) and loads the final index prices used to settle financial trades.

error.defect_description: A delivered volume is taken from the wrong NSI or allocation.

evidence.note: Physical bilateral power settles through net settlement instructions registered with the AESO (guide section 5.1). The wait is from capture to the end of the first delivery month: prompt-month and balance-of-month trades settle within weeks, forward strips months later (author's estimate).

steps.name: Prepare the netting statement or invoice
steps.description: The ETRM settlement module computes the amount due on each trade for the month; the analyst checks it, nets payables and receivables with each counterparty as the master agreement allows, and emails the statement or invoice by the agreed day early in the month.

error.defect_description: A trade is left out of the netting statement or an old price is used.

evidence.note: Month-end statement practice estimated.

steps.name: Counterparty sends its own statement
steps.description: The counterparty's settlement desk sends its statement or invoice for the same month, which may arrive before or after the company's own and may net trades differently.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Compare the two statements
steps.description: The analyst compares the counterparty's statement with the company's line by line on volume, price and amount, and either agrees it or lists the differences to resolve before the payment date.

next.condition: difference in price, volume or trade list

evidence.note: Difference rate estimated.

steps.name: Reconcile the exchange settlement statement
steps.description: For exchange-cleared trades the analyst reconciles the exchange's monthly settlement statement with the ETRM settlement amounts, including fees and any physical delivery adjustments, and lists any differences.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Resolve the settlement difference
steps.description: The analyst works the difference with the counterparty's or exchange's settlement staff, checking trade lists, index prices and delivered volumes, and agrees a corrected statement or an adjustment in the next month.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Approve the settlement payments
steps.description: The manager reviews the monthly payment and receipt list by counterparty, checks large or unusual amounts against the agreed statements, and approves the payment run sent to treasury.

control.basis: Payments policy: settlement approves amounts, treasury releases funds

evidence.note: Touch time is the trade's share of a batch approval.

steps.name: Release payment or confirm receipt
steps.description: On the payment date set by the master agreement or the exchange, the treasury analyst releases wires for net payables and confirms that receivables arrived, chasing late payers through the credit team.

evidence.note: Payment date around the 20th of the month after delivery is common in North American master agreements but was not confirmed in an opened source.

steps.name: Apply cash and post settlement entries
steps.description: The analyst matches cash received and paid to open receivables and payables in the ERP, clears the realised trading amounts and uploads the journal entries for the month-end close.

error.defect_description: Cash applied to the wrong counterparty or month.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (NI 52-109 and SOX 404): reconciliation of trading settlements to cash and ledger

next.condition: trade settled for the delivery month and posted

evidence.note: Estimated.

exceptions.name: Mis-booked trade
exceptions.description: The company's ETRM booking differs from what was agreed; the trader amends it and the trade is rechecked and reconfirmed.

exceptions.name: Disputed trade terms
exceptions.description: Both sides believe different terms were agreed; managers resolve it from recordings and broker records, sometimes cancelling the trade.

exceptions.name: Settlement statement difference
exceptions.description: Counterparty statement differs on price, volume or trade list; the analyst resolves it and reissues the statement.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from trade capture to cash settlement of the first delivery month
benchmarks.population: Power and gas trades of an Alberta generator's hedging desk

evidence.note: Author's estimate: a prompt-month trade made mid-month delivers over the next month, is invoiced early in the month after and paid around the 20th (about 45 days); forward strips starting several months out lengthen the tail.

benchmarks.unit: share of trades submitted to ICE eConfirm

evidence.note: Vendor statement, not an independent study.

pain_points.description: Paper confirmations wait days for counterparties to countersign, and unconfirmed trades sit on ageing reports that credit and audit follow up.

evidence.note: The ICE fact sheet contrasts minutes for electronic matching with the manual paper process; the waits are the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Month-end concentrates hundreds of trade settlements into the first two weeks of the month, and statement differences must be worked out before the payment date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Physical power trades must agree with net settlement instructions in the AESO system, so a trade error shows up again in AESO settlement.

assumptions: The unit of work is one trade followed to the settlement of its first delivery month; touch times at month-end steps are the trade's share of batch work.
Interface shares assume most trades start from the company's own booking (hedging process); exchange-sourced and counterparty-first trades are smaller shares.
Credit exposure is produced for every trade, so that interface uses outcome 'any'; the payment request to treasury is added beyond the organisation file's links.
Payment dates come from master agreements and exchange rules that were not opened; the 20th-of-month practice is tier C.
No physical resources, travel or field wait causes apply to this office process.

sources.title: Information Document: Power Pool Settlement Guide, ID #2011-002R
sources.supports: Preliminary power pool statements by the end of the 5th business day after the settlement period and final statements by the 15th; payments based on final statements and settled by wire on the 20th business day; statement line items (energy payment, trading charge, PSM, TCR, dispatch down service, prior period adjustments, participation fee, interest); verification reports in the Energy Trading System (metered volumes updated 5 business days after production, NSI reports, settlement changes, PFAM summary); generator discrepancies go to the meter data manager, other queries to settlement@aeso.ca; each production month settled at 1 month (initial), 2 months (interim) and 4 months (final); written disputes on final statements under section 103.2; final amount must be paid in full despite a dispute.

sources.title: ICE eConfirm fact sheet
sources.supports: Electronic matching of energy trade confirmations for physical and financial trades on and off exchange, including voice-brokered and bilateral trades; 95 percent of submitted trades matched within minutes; input by web form, file upload or XML API; users review confirmed trades and resolve discrepancies; manual paper confirmation is the alternative.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Energy Marketing negotiates contracts with customers for the output of the generation assets and trades power, gas and environmental products; about 50 percent of capacity contracted in 2022 and 2023 and uncontracted merchant positions regularly hedged; Dow contract extension with a 10-year initial term from January 1, 2020; 18-year 100 MW renewable PPA with Pembina for Garden Plain and the remaining 30 MW marketed to commercial and industrial customers; counterparty credit limits monitored and collateral required above credit limits.
